artworks.title: The sea-god Nereus seated on a shell with his daughters
artworks.description: Philips Galle's engraving visualises the Nereid brood born to Nereus and Doris: the Old Man of the Sea enthroned on a great shell while his daughters crowd behind him. Doris herself is rarely depicted alone in Western art; Renaissance print series like this one made the couple's progeny the visible face of the genealogy Hesiod and Apollodorus spell out in catalogue form.

artworks.title: Nereus, Doris, and Oceanus on the Pergamon Altar
artworks.description: West frieze of the Great Altar of Pergamon (Pergamonmuseum, Berlin): Doris fights beside her husband Nereus and her father Oceanus against the Giants in the Gigantomachy. The Oceanid who mothers the Nereids appears here as a warrior consort — one of the few monumental ancient portraits that name her in the cosmomachy rather than only in a genealogical list.

artworks.title: Doris in the Sea Thiasos (Altar of Domitius Ahenobarbus)
artworks.description: Relief detail from the so-called Altar of Domitius Ahenobarbus (Glyptothek Munich, inv. 239): Doris, mother of the bride Amphitrite, carries two torches to light the marine wedding procession of Poseidon and Amphitrite. The Roman-era sea thiasos makes the Oceanid visible as matron of the Nereid line — torch-bearer for her daughter's marriage to the sea-king.

popCulture.title: Doris (Oceanid)
popCulture.description: Doris endures as Nereus' rich-haired consort — mother of the fifty Nereids and the Oceanid who stocked the Aegean with sea-nymphs.
